question: If tan² A - 6 tan A + 9 = 0, 0 sqrt{10} cos A?
solution:
**Given:**

tan2A - 6tanA + 9 = 0

**Concept used:**

tanθ = P/B

cotθ = 1/tanθ

cosθ = B/H

Here,

P = Perpendicular

B = Base

H = Hypotenuse 

Pythagoras theorem = H2 = P2 + B2

**Calculation:**

tan2A - 6tanA + 9 = 0

⇒ tan2A - 2 × 3 × tanA + 9 = 0

⇒ (tanA - 3)² = 0

⇒ (tanA - 3) = 0

⇒ tanA = 3

So, P/B = 3/1

Now,

H² = 3² + 1²

⇒ H2 = 9 + 1

⇒ H2 = 10

⇒ H = √10

So, cosA = 1/√10

Now,

6 cot A + 8√{10} cos A = 6 × (1/3) + 8√{10} × (1/√10)

⇒ 2 + 8

⇒ 10

**∴ Required answer is 10.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**

tan2A - 6tanA + 9 = 0

⇒ (tanA - 3)2 = 0

⇒ (tanA - 3) = 0

⇒ tanA = 3

⇒ cotA = 1/3

cosA = 1 ÷ sqrt{sec²A}

⇒ 1 ÷sqrt{1 + tan²A}

⇒ 1 ÷sqrt{1 + 9} = frac {1}{sqrt{10}}

Now,

6 cot A + 8sqrt{10} cos A

⇒ 6 × (1/3) + 8sqrt{10} × frac {1}{sqrt{10}}

⇒ 2 + 8 = 10

**∴ The value of 6 cot A + 8sqrt{10} cos A is 10.**
